name: Turn an agentskills.io SKILL.md Folder Into a Conductor Agent — CLI skill run / load / serve and Python skill()
query: We have an agentskills.io skill folder at `./skills/release-notes` (a `SKILL.md`, a `scripts/collect_prs.py`, and a sub-agent file). I'd like to (a) try it once from the CLI with GPT-4o-mini, (b) deploy it so the UI can run it by name, and (c) call it as a tool from our existing Python `tech_lead` agent. Anything special about big SKILL.md files or the server?
expected_behavior: Step 1: Consult references/cli-index.md (Skills table: `conductor skill run {path-or-name} "prompt" --model provider/model [--param k=v] [--workspace dir]`, `skill load {path} --model ...` deploys as an agent with framework `skill`, `skill serve {path-or-name}`, `skill register {path} [--version] [--model] [--agent-model name=model]`, `skill list/get/pull/delete`; requires `agentspan.skills.enabled=true`, off by default; after `load`, `conductor agent run --name {skill}` works), references/agents.md §2 (path 4c — skill agent) and §12 (`/api/skills/**` needs `agentspan.skills.enabled=true`), references/agent-sdks.md §7 (`skill("path", model=M)` → `Agent`; `agent_tool(dg, description=...)`; `load_skills(dir)`), references/optimization.md F1, F3, F6, and SKILL.md Rule 13 (no `conductor deploy`).

Step 2: (a) One-off: `conductor skill run ./skills/release-notes "Write the release notes for v2.3" --model openai/gpt-4o-mini` (optionally `--param repo=acme/api --workspace ./work`) — the CLI process serves the skill's script tools for the duration of the run.

Step 3: (b) Deploy: `conductor skill load ./skills/release-notes --model openai/gpt-4o-mini` registers the skill as a deployed agent (framework `skill`); then `conductor agent run --name release-notes "..."`, the UI `/runAgent`, or an `AGENT` task can start it. Because `scripts/collect_prs.py` becomes a worker tool named `release-notes__collect_prs` (`<skill>__<script>`), a `conductor skill serve ./skills/release-notes` (or `conductor skill serve release-notes`) process must be running for runs started from the UI or a workflow (Rule 9 / F3). `--agent-model name=provider/model` overrides the model of a sub-agent.

Step 4: Optional `conductor skill register ./skills/release-notes --version 1.0.0 --model openai/gpt-4o-mini` stores the package server-side via `/api/skills`; this needs `agentspan.skills.enabled=true` on the server (off by default) — check with `conductor skill list`.

Step 5: (c) Python: `from conductor.ai.agents import Agent, AgentRuntime, skill, agent_tool`; `rn = skill("./skills/release-notes", model="openai/gpt-4o-mini")` returns an `Agent`; `tech_lead = Agent(name="tech_lead", model="openai/gpt-4o-mini", instructions="...", tools=[agent_tool(rn, description="Draft release notes for a version")], max_turns=10)`; `runtime.deploy(tech_lead)` in CI and a long-lived `runtime.serve(tech_lead, rn)` (or `conductor skill serve`) so the skill's script workers are served — the `agent_tool` itself needs no worker.
Step 6: Package mapping: `scripts/` → `<skill>__<script>` worker tools; sub-agent files → `agent_tool`s; SKILL.md sections are split above 50 KB.

Step 7: Model is always `--model provider/model` / `model="provider/model"` (F6); never `conductor deploy`; any `AGENT` task uses `agentType: "conductor"` + `name: "release-notes"` (or inline `skillRef{name,version}`) — never `agentType: "skill"` (`skill` is the framework id, not an execution mode). Bounds: `max_turns` on `tech_lead`, `maxDurationSeconds` on callers (F1).
success_criteria: Shows `conductor skill run ./skills/release-notes "<prompt>" --model openai/gpt-4o-mini` (provider-qualified) for the one-off try
Shows `conductor skill load <path> --model provider/model` to deploy (framework `skill`), followed by `conductor agent run --name release-notes ...` / the UI
States that `conductor skill serve <path-or-name>` must be running for runs started from the UI or a workflow, because `scripts/` become worker tools
States that scripts map to worker tools named `<skill>__<script>` (e.g. `release-notes__collect_prs`) and that sub-agent files become `agent_tool`s
States that `conductor skill register` / `/api/skills` needs `agentspan.skills.enabled=true` (off by default)
Python path uses `skill("./skills/release-notes", model=...)` returning an `Agent`, wrapped with `agent_tool(rn, description=...)` in `tech_lead`'s `tools`
Does not invent a SKILL.md size limit; if size is discussed, states the real behaviour (bodies over 50,000 characters are auto-split into `## ` sections) — N/A and passing when size is not discussed
Never uses `conductor deploy`; the SDK `runtime.deploy` / `runtime.serve` (or `conductor skill serve`) handles deployment and serving
If an `AGENT` task is shown, it uses `agentType: "conductor"` + `name` (or `skillRef`) — never `agentType: "skill"` or another framework name; N/A and passing when no AGENT task is shown
